resolutions.researcher_notes: P6713 and P1855 are NOT simple duplicates of each other, but P6713 IS a genuine misclassification. Multiple independent sources agree the Bahr Essalam (Sabratha platform) field is tied to Mellitah by exactly TWO separate subsea lines, not one: a 36-in line carrying GAS and a 10-in line carrying CONDENSATE (liquids). Offshore Technology: '10-in diameter pipeline through which condensate is directly pumped and conveyed to Mellitah'; Offshore Magazine: '36-in. and 10-in. pipelines taking gas and condensate from the platform 100-km south to Mellitah.' P6713 has diameter=10in — it IS the condensate line, not a second gas line, despite carrying the same 'Gas Pipeline' name as P1855 (diameter=36in, the true gas line). The likely mechanical origin of the GEM duplication: OPEC's own ASB tables list BOTH diameters under one shared row/label ('Bahr Assalam/Mellitah ... 68.2 mi ... 36 in ... 9,199,943' and a second row 'Bahr Assalam/Mellitah ... 68.2 mi ... 10 in ... 465,166', both under the 'Gas pipelines' table heading even though the 10-in line is physically condensate) — someone appears to have carried both OPEC rows into GGIT as two separate 'Gas Pipeline' entities instead of recognizing the second as condensate. Critically, GEM ALREADY tracks this exact 10-in condensate line correctly, under GOIT (oil/NGL tracker): P6457 'Sabratha-Mellitah Condensate Pipeline' — Start='Sabratha platform', End='Mellitah', Length=107 km, Diameter=10 in, Status=operating — near-identical specs to P6713 (Bahr Assalam/Mellitah, 109 km, 10 in, operating). FINDING: P6713 in GGIT (gas) is a duplicate/misclassified twin of P6457 in GOIT (oil/NGL); it belongs in the oil tracker, not the gas tracker, and once reclassified is redundant with the already-existing P6457. Recommend retiring/removing P6713 from GGIT (or merging its provenance into P6457) rather than treating it as a distinct gas pipeline needing its own refs going forward.
